winner.text: Use inverse user-impression-count weights in binary cross-entropy so highly active users do not dominate training updates.
winner.rationale: Official nDCG@5 is macro-averaged across users, whereas unweighted row loss gives more influence to users with many training impressions. User-frequency segments show differentiated behavior, so a user-balanced loss is a ranking-aligned training ablation.
winner.exact_ablation: Replace only unweighted binary cross-entropy in experiment 1 with binary cross-entropy weighted by the reciprocal of each user's count of training impressions, normalized to mean weight one; retain all model, feature, optimizer, seed, and schedule settings unchanged.

expected_effect.GAUC: -0.0003 to +0.0015 because user balancing may trade dominant-user fit for macro ordering.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: +0.0000 to +0.0020 because the training weighting better matches macro per-user top-five evaluation.

selection_rationale: Select c09: inverse user-impression-count BCE weighting is the consultant's top-ranked scarce-run option (utility 0.66) and is a single, low-runtime, leakage-safe ablation. It directly addresses the mismatch between row-weighted BCE and macro per-user nDCG@5/within-user evaluation, with plausible support from differentiated user-frequency behavior. Its expected primary gain (+0.0008) is modest but credible relative to its limited downside. c01 is a known rollback to experiment 1 rather than a new experiment, while higher-upside loss or architecture replacements have materially greater implementation, runtime, and validation-overfitting risk.
